population: Previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (zimberelimab and geptanolimab trials PD-L1-positive only)
note: Four later anti-PD-1 antibodies entered cervical cancer on pembrolizumab's precedent; only zimberelimab published monkey occupancy and a mouse tumour model before its cervical readout, and both held; balstilimab and geptanolimab preclinical data are unpublished.

engagement.model: Cynomolgus PD-1 receptor occupancy on blood T cells (zimberelimab)
engagement.note: Zimberelimab saturated PD-1 on activated cynomolgus T cells at every dose from 5 mg/kg before patient dosing.
engagement.quote: After an intravenous injection of GLS-010, the RO rate on the D50 were saturated in the cynomolgus monkeys in the low-, moderate-, and high-dose groups, compared with the control group

engagement.magnitude_basis: peripheral T-cell PD-1 occupancy: ~93-95% (CD3+, day 50) in monkeys vs >80% in phase Ia patients
engagement.population: Advanced solid tumours or lymphoma (phase Ia, any histology)

engagement.judgement: Occupancy on blood T cells is a direct readout. Engagement pools patients of any tumour type, so the phase Ia (not cervical) counts.
engagement.model: Cynomolgus PD-1 receptor occupancy on blood T cells (zimberelimab)
engagement.note: The same paper sets saturated monkey PD-1 occupancy beside >80% occupancy in phase Ia patients with advanced tumours.
engagement.short: Human PD-1 occupancy >80%, as in monkeys
engagement.quote: After intravenous infusion, the RO rate could reach saturation within a short time. A phase Ia study showed a RO of >80% in humans (27).

dose.population: Previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (zimberelimab and geptanolimab trials PD-L1-positive only)
dose.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the first member cervical trial with a published preclinical package (zimberelimab NCT03972722) started 2019-05-15; the cynomolgus and mouse work predates it and was published in September 2021.
dose.note: Monkeys tolerated zimberelimab for 26 weeks without findings and saturated PD-1 at 5 mg/kg, the basis offered for clinical dosing.
dose.short: Monkey margin and occupancy before patients
dose.quote: No abnormal manifestation was observed in the animals in the 26 continuous weeks dosing study

dose.magnitude_basis: tolerated human dose range (to 10 mg/kg Q2W) against a 26-week monkey study without findings
dose.population: Advanced solid tumours or lymphoma (phase Ia, any histology)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level for the phase Ia (EJC, paywalled). Monkey repeat-dose levels for the 26-week study are not stated in the preclinical paper; single doses to 1000 mg/kg were given.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the monkey package stated a tolerability margin (no findings over 26 weeks, saturated occupancy at the lowest 5 mg/kg dose) but no explicit human exposure target, so this scores the margin half only (margin_stated true). Paired: the phase Ia paper says the dose drew on preclinical data but does not set the two side by side. Grade >=3 TEAEs (39.8%) were mostly disease-related cytopenias and liver tests, with grade >=3 irAEs 4.5%, not a dose-limiting toxicity.
dose.note: Phase Ia dosed 1-10 mg/kg and 240 mg without a dose-limiting toxicity; 240 mg Q2W chosen partly on preclinical data.
dose.short: No DLT to 10 mg/kg; margin held
dose.quote: DLT was not observed in phase Ia part.

dose.quote: The Q3W flat dose was selected based on population PK modeling along with efficacy and safety data on weight-based regimens from the BCD-100-2/MIRACULUM study (NCT03269565).
dose.judgement: Opening entry at first use. Not a retrodiction: the model was fitted to weight-based PK but predicted exposure for a regimen not yet given to anyone.
dose.model: BIOCAD population PK model simulating a 250 mg Q3W flat dose of prolgolimab

dose.population: Untreated unresectable or metastatic melanoma (FLAT); dose pools tumour types
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11408354). The comparison is with a historical control (MIRACULUM) and the authors caution that bioanalytical methods differed between studies. FLAT has no registry results.
dose.note: Observed flat-dose troughs exceeded weight-based troughs, as the popPK simulation predicted; melanoma patients, not cervical.
dose.quote: Figure 4  illustrates that Ctrough values with flat dosing were consistently higher to weight-based dosing in the overall Ctrough population.
dose.reason: Flat-dose troughs met the predicted exposure
dose.judgement: Dose question scored on exposure only; the non-inferior ORR belongs to efficacy in melanoma, outside this tile. Dose pools tumour types as patient PK, so a melanoma trial counts. No tolerability margin was stated by the model, so margin_stated false. The cervical trials (CAESURA, FERMATA) used weight-based dosing, so this track bears on the class's dosing, not on the cervical readouts.
dose.model: BIOCAD population PK model simulating a 250 mg Q3W flat dose of prolgolimab

efficacy.note: Zimberelimab 10-20 mg/kg inhibited MC38 growth in hPD-1 knock-in mice; no cervical model was used.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: tumour growth inhibition in mice vs single-arm objective response rate
efficacy.population: Previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (zimberelimab and geptanolimab trials PD-L1-positive only)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Registry NCT03972722 status unknown, no results posted. The Simon two-stage null rate is not in the abstract, so whether the design's bar was formally cleared is unverified.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: a colon syngeneic model predicts only that PD-1 blockade shrinks tumours, so the match is direction only and low confidence; the model was not cervical. Kept as a track because it is the only member's tumour model with public data before a cervical trial read out.
efficacy.model: MC38 colon tumours in human PD-1 knock-in mice (zimberelimab)
efficacy.note: Zimberelimab gave a 27.6% IRC-assessed response rate in 105 PD-L1-positive previously treated cervical cancers, its primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: The objective response rate was 27.6%, and the disease control rate was 55.2%.

patient_trials.quote: Zimberelimab monotherapy demonstrated durable anti-tumor activity and an acceptable safety profile in patients with cervical cancer.

efficacy.population: Previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (zimberelimab and geptanolimab trials PD-L1-positive only)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Model year is a proxy (prolgolimab cervical trials started 2019; the mouse comparison was published in 2024). FERMATA (NCT03912415) registry status unknown, no results posted. CAESURA quote from the ASCO 2023 abstract via a secondary listing, not read in JCO.
efficacy.judgement: Judgement call: CAESURA (single-arm prolgolimab + platinum doublet + bevacizumab, ORR 63.8%) cannot isolate the antibody's contribution, so it changes no status; the randomised FERMATA OS readout would. Not marked a retrodiction because the mouse study's run date is not stated.
efficacy.model: CT26 colon tumours in mice (prolgolimab vs pembrolizumab)
efficacy.note: Prolgolimab inhibited CT26 growth 56% vs 16% for pembrolizumab; its cervical phase 3 (FERMATA, OS) has no public result.
efficacy.quote: An in vivo study in mice inoculated with CT26.wt cancer cells showed that tumor growth inhibition was 16% for pembrolizumab and 56% for prolgolimab.

patient_trials.quote: ORR per iRECIST was 70.7% (41 of 58 pts) with 2 complete and 39 partial responses.

safety.population: Previously treated recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer (zimberelimab and geptanolimab trials PD-L1-positive only)
safety.confidence_note: Year is a proxy: the first member cervical trial with a published preclinical package (zimberelimab NCT03972722) started 2019-05-15; the cynomolgus and mouse work predates it and was published in September 2021. The study report itself is unpublished; the paper gives one summary paragraph and does not list thyroid function among the endpoints.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: not scored contra. The monkey study named no harm, and immune-mediated thyroiditis or colitis from PD-1 blockade alone needs a pre-existing autoreactive or tumour context that healthy monkeys lack, so its silence is treated like a mouse's silence on cytokine release. Patient side: hypothyroidism 26.7% (Xia 2023), grade >=3 irAE 4.5% (Liu 2021).
safety.note: Healthy monkeys showed no findings over 26 weeks; patients had immune-mediated hypothyroidism (26.7%), a harm healthy monkeys rarely show under PD-1 blockade alone.
safety.quote: No abnormal manifestation was observed in the animals in the 26 continuous weeks dosing study
safety.reason: Monkeys named no harm to check
